scope: Pandora Operations Room routing, live enterprise-context compatibility, and protected merge recovery

defects.verifiedFact: The UI advertised @room but source had no first-class @room parser. Ambiguous @room requests could therefore fall through to Athena instead of summoning a bounded specialist team.
defects.repair: Added case-insensitive operationsRoomRequestsTeam parsing. Ambiguous @room requests now summon HERMES, HEPHAESTUS, and ARTEMIS; explicit specialist mentions retain precedence.

defects.verifiedFact: The mobile Operations Room supplied 13 selectedObject entries while live pandora-intelligence-chat rejects enterprise selectedObject values with more than 8 entries.
defects.repair: Reduced selectedObject to exactly eight fields and consolidated architecture/model policy into architecturePolicy and localModel without weakening the phone-local and infrastructure constraints.

coordinatorIncident.symptom: A successful generation-1 provider check was recorded while the repository fence remained stranded in publishing, blocking merge claim. After its expiry, generation 2 hit CHECK_PROGRESS_READBACK_MISMATCH because GitHub preserved completed/success while accepting the new generation external_id instead of regressing a completed check to in_progress.
recovery: Released the stranded generation-1 publishing fence only after exact provider/check/state invariants proved the successful publication receipt had already been recorded.
Published a fresh generation-2 decision against the unchanged main/head and authoritative snapshot.
Read back the generation-2 external_id from GitHub and observed the check already in the stronger final completed/success state.

Reconciled that final provider state into the coordinator ledger with record_publish_v2, released the publication fence, claimed the merge fence, merged the exact reviewed head with SHA guard, and completed the merge from provider readback.

temporaryTransport.fact: A retired Supabase function slot was temporarily used as a hard-bound GitHub App reviewer transport because the ordinary connector authenticated as the PR author and could not satisfy independent approval.
temporaryTransport.bounds: The temporary implementation was fixed to PR 710 and exact head 94d58115b131299c8fa5eff63df228f0ea3c573f, used server-side GitHub App material only, and never returned private key/token material.

releaseBoundary.note: The live pandora-intelligence-chat backend already enforced the eight-field contract; the merged mobile source now conforms to it.

durableLessons: UI affordances that advertise orchestration syntax must have deterministic parser coverage; do not rely on prompt wording to make commands such as @room real.
Client enterprise-context schemas must be contract-tested against the live backend field-count and validation limits; source-only structural tests should catch drift before runtime.
Post-provider reconciliation must accept a stronger already-terminal provider state when a provider refuses or ignores a status regression but has applied the new exact identity/idempotency metadata.
A provider mutation can succeed before local orchestration finishes. After any ambiguous post-provider failure, read provider truth first and reconcile; do not blindly retry the mutation.
Repository fences need explicit recovery for the state where publication receipt is durably recorded but the publishing fence was not released.

Never weaken protected-branch rules to finish a merge. Satisfy independent review, exact-head checks, coordinator PASS, merge claim, provider SHA-guarded merge, completion readback, and final main SHA verification.

provenance.github: PR 710, exact-head check runs, independent GitHub App approvals, provider merge response, and final main readback
provenance.supabase: live pandora-intelligence-chat source/readback, coordinator state/fence/readback, and Vault-backed GitHub transport
provenance.classification: verified facts and generalized failure/recovery lessons; no customer/private credential material
